judged.reason: The restatement ends 'but will only show what the text means.' The quotation says only what Pico will not do (imitate those who heap together authorities); his positive alternative is not stated in the quoted lines.
judged.suggested_text: Pico says he will not imitate those who, in explaining creation, have heaped together whatever philosophers or theologians have said about God, the angels, matter and the heavens, and that Isaac the Persian and Samuel Ophinides particularly sinned in this among the Hebrews.

judged.suggested_text: Pico cites the Chaldeans' injunction not to exaggerate fate as a warning against overrating stellar influence, and himself urges that goods of body or fortune should not be sought from the heavens, which will not give them, but from the Lord of heaven.

judged.suggested_text: Pico says the angels can be raised to the true felicity, the contemplation of the face of God, but cannot ascend to it, Lucifer having sinned in saying he would ascend, and that the divine power making men and angels pleasing to God is called grace.
